title: A non-sealed extension point for commands

blocks.text: A `non-sealed` permitted subclass opens the hierarchy at one chosen point. `Commands` uses that to give a closed command set one extension point:

items: `sealed interface Command permits Quit, Echo, Extension`;
`abstract non-sealed class Extension` with two abstract methods, `String name()` and `String run()`. Anyone may extend it; the library ships one, `Help`.

blocks.text: Write `static String execute(Command c)` with a `switch` over the command:
The library cannot list every extension, because it does not know them: the switch handles them all through the methods `Extension` declares.

cases.says: Quit, Echo and the built-in Help extension each produce their output.
A subclass of the non-sealed Extension that the library has never seen still runs, through its own name and run methods.

concepts: A non-sealed subclass is a chosen extension point: subclasses the library never saw match its case and are handled through its abstract methods.
